title: Etale local representation and null-homotopy for finite free sources
statement: Let $U$ be a scheme with small etale site $U_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], let $B$ be a commutative ring, let $P^\bullet$ be a bounded cochain complex of finite free $B$-modules (each $P^i$ is isomorphic to $B^{r_i}$ for some $r_i\in\mathbb N$), and let $\mathcal F^\bullet$ be any cochain complex of sheaves of $\underline B$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $\underline{P}^\bullet$ for the termwise constant sheaf complex [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and $Q$ for localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. (1) Every morphism $\varphi:Q(\underline P^\bullet)\to Q(\mathcal F^\bullet)$ in $D(U_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ is represented, after an etale covering $\{V_j\to U\}$, by chain maps $\alpha_j:\underline P^\bullet|_{V_j}\to\mathcal F^\bullet|_{V_j}$. (2) If a chain map $\alpha:\underline P^\bullet\to\mathcal F^\bullet$ has $Q(\alpha)=0$, there is an etale covering on which it is null-homotopic: on each member there are sheaf morphisms $h^i:\underline P^i\to\mathcal F^{i-1}$ satisfying $\alpha^i=d_{\mathcal F}^{i-1}h^i+h^{i+1}d_P^i$ for every $i$.

source.place: Tag 08FR, lemma-local-actual, assertions (1) and (2), specialized to the ringed small etale site with coefficient sheaf the constant ring B

proof.text: Put $R=\underline B$ and $E=\underline P^\bullet$. Sheafifying the chosen bases $P^i\cong B^{r_i}$ gives $E^i\cong R^{\oplus r_i}$: sheafification preserves finite coproducts, and the component maps and inverse maps still compose to the identity. It also preserves the zero terms, so $E$ has the same finite support interval. For every $i$, [lem-sc-finite-free-internal-hom-exact-sequence] gives exactness of $\mathcal Hom_R(E^i,-)$ at the middle of any exact short complex. Apply it to the three exact short complexes $(0,S_1,S_2)$, $(S_1,S_2,S_3)$ and $(S_2,S_3,0)$ of a short exact sequence. Since $\mathcal Hom_R(E^i,0)=0$, these give respectively injectivity, middle exactness and surjectivity. Thus each termwise internal Hom functor preserves short exact sequences, including when $r_i=0$.

source.place: Tag 08FR (lemma-local-actual), finite-free specialization; Tag 08FN (lemma-local-lift-map), basis calculation

proof.text: Use the two-universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]: schemes and coefficients lie in $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$, the site is replaced by its $\mathcal V$-small skeleton, and sheaves and derived categories are formed in $\mathcal V$. On this small ringed site, apply [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] to the sheaf of commutative rings $R$ and the arbitrary complex $\mathcal F$, obtaining a quasi-isomorphism $q:\mathcal F\to I$ with $I$ K-injective. No lower or upper bound on $\mathcal F$ is used. Set $H_M=\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(E,M)$, with the differential of [def-pur-hom-complex]. The bounded source and termwise exactness proved in step 1 meet every hypothesis of [lem-pc-bounded-exact-term-hom-quasi-iso]. Hence $H_q:H_{\mathcal F}\to H_I$ is a quasi-isomorphism of sheaf complexes.

source.place: Section 07A5 (section-unbounded), K-injective resolutions; Section 0A8X (section-hom-complexes); Tag 08FR, construction of representatives

proof.text: Each section group of $H_M$ is a $B$-module via the canonical constant-section map $B\to R(V)$; restrictions commute with this action. Define a presheaf of $B$-modules $A_M(V)=H^0(H_M(V))$ on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$. By [def-pur-hom-complex], a degree-zero cycle is precisely a chain map $E|_V\to M|_V$; a degree-minus-one element $h$ has $d(h)=d_Mh+hd_E$. Thus $A_M(V)$ is the group of chain maps modulo chain homotopy, naturally in $V$ and $M$. The exact forgetful functor of [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] identifies cohomology in $R$-module sheaves with underlying abelian-sheaf cohomology. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] to the presheaf complex underlying $H_M$: its termwise sheafification is itself, and exact sheafification gives $A_M^\#\cong H^0(H_M)$ on underlying abelian sheaves. Consequently step 2 gives an isomorphism $A_{\mathcal F}^\#\to A_I^\#$. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-iso-locally-bijective], the presheaf map $A_{\mathcal F}\to A_I$ is locally surjective and locally injective. This is about homotopy classes of actual maps, not about sections of a cohomology sheaf before choosing representatives.

source.place: Section 0A8X, equation cohomology-hom-complex; literature/stacks-project/sites.tex Tags 00WJ and 00WK, exact sheafification and local sections

proof.text: For an etale object $V\to U$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open] identifies $(U_{\mathrm{et}})/V$ with $V_{\mathrm{et}}$, including the covering families. With the ring and its action carried along, [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] describes module restriction sectionwise. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-restriction-exact] restriction is exact on underlying abelian sheaves; applying the faithful exact forgetful functor of [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful] on both sites shows that it is exact on module sheaves too. It therefore preserves kernels, images and their quotient cohomology objects, and in particular takes $q$ to a quasi-isomorphism $q|_V$. It preserves the displayed homotopy equation simply by restricting each component. Thus it induces restriction on derived categories, and $Q(q|_V)$ is invertible.

proof.text: Given $\varphi:QE\to Q\mathcal F$, the surjectivity of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] supplies a chain map $\beta:E\to I$ with $Q\beta=Qq\circ\varphi$. View its homotopy class as $[\beta]\in A_I(U)$. Local surjectivity in step 3 supplies an etale covering $\{V_j\to U\}$ and classes $a_j\in A_{\mathcal F}(V_j)$ sent to $[\beta|_{V_j}]$. Choose a chain-map representative $\alpha_j$ of each $a_j$. The equality of classes means $q|_{V_j}\circ\alpha_j$ and $\beta|_{V_j}$ differ by $d_Ih+hd_E$ for an actual degree-minus-one family $h$, so they have the same image in the derived category. Step 4 makes $Q(q|_{V_j})$ invertible; cancel it in $Q(q|_{V_j})\circ Q\alpha_j=Q\beta|_{V_j}=Q(q|_{V_j})\circ\varphi|_{V_j}$. Hence $Q\alpha_j=\varphi|_{V_j}$, proving (1).

source.place: Tag 08FR (lemma-local-actual), assertion (1); literature/stacks-project/derived.tex Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective), Hom bijection

proof.text: Now suppose $\alpha:E\to\mathcal F$ has $Q\alpha=0$. Then $Q(q\alpha)=0$. The injectivity of [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] implies that $q\alpha$ is null-homotopic on $U$, so $[\alpha]$ and $0$ in $A_{\mathcal F}(U)$ have equal images in $A_I(U)$. Local injectivity in step 3 gives an etale covering $\{V_j\to U\}$ with $[\alpha|_{V_j}]=0$ in $A_{\mathcal F}(V_j)$. Being zero in this cohomology group means an actual boundary, not merely a zero sheaf cohomology class: choose $h_j\in H_{\mathcal F}^{-1}(V_j)$ with $d(h_j)=\alpha|_{V_j}$. The degree-minus-one differential formula yields $\alpha^i|_{V_j}=d_{\mathcal F}^{i-1}h_j^i+h_j^{i+1}d_E^i$ for every $i$. The one element $h_j$ supplies all components simultaneously. This proves (2), including the zero source and empty scheme cases, where the equation is vacuous.
